rows.description: Capacitance of an ion cyclotron heating antenna is the non-negative charge-to-voltage proportionality of a specified lumped impedance-matching element in the antenna RF circuit.

Co-passing fast-particle current density is the signed conventional electric-charge flux per unit area carried by fast particles on co-passing, untrapped guiding-center orbits. It is a vector orbit-class contribution and excludes compensating electron and thermal-ion return currents.
Torque density vector giving the angular-momentum source per unit volume deposited by Coulomb collisions on co-passing fast ions in a specified charge state.

Collisional co-passing torque density for fast ions is the local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to or from the co-passing fast-ion population caused by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species.
Co-passing collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per plasma volume to a specified thermal ion charge state from Coulomb collisions with co-passing particles.

Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, restricted to co-passing orbit-class contributions and without restricting spatial direction.

Co-passing torque density due to j cross b force is the vector density of angular-momentum transfer produced by the Lorentz force acting on the co-passing plasma population. It is the parent concept for co-passing directionally projected forms.
Current density is the vector flux density of conventional electric charge, equal to electric current per unit area normal to the flow.
Electric current density contributed by counter-passing fast particles on guiding-center orbits, excluding thermal and compensating return-current contributions.
Volumetric counter-passing torque density deposited in the fast-electron population through Coulomb collisions, the local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume.
Collisional torque-density vector transferred to counter-passing fast ions in a specified charge state by Coulomb collisions with background plasma particles.
Collisional counter-passing torque density for fast ions is the local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions.
Counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate to bulk thermal electrons from Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles.

Counter-passing collisional torque density is the vector angular-momentum transfer rate per plasma volume delivered to a specified thermal ion charge state from Coulomb collisions with counter-passing particles.
Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated by the Lorentz force, averaged over a magnetic flux surface for counter-passing particles.
Vector density of electric current carried by a specified charged-particle contribution, obtained from its signed charge-weighted particle flux.
Effective velocity multiplying electron particle density in the density-proportional convective part of electron particle transport.
Peak plasma energy deposition per unit surface area, defined as the spatial maximum of the corresponding energy flux over a plasma-facing surface.
Fast-electron collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to fast electrons through Coulomb collisions.
Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified fast (non-thermal) ion charge state within the plasma volume enclosed by a selected magnetic flux surface.
Volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer to fast ions of a specified charge state, aggregated over co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped orbit classes.
Fast-ion collisional torque density is the local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to fast ions per unit plasma volume caused by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species.

Flux-surface averaged toroidal flux coordinate gradient magnitude is the flux-surface average of the magnitude of the spatial gradient of the toroidal flux coordinate. It is the metric factor for how rapidly that coordinate label changes across neighboring flux surfaces.

Forward wave phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna is the phase of the forward RF power-wave phasor for one antenna module, referenced to the first module to define toroidal phasing; positive phase advances toward increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
Photon-number radiance from an impurity-ion spectral line produced by charge exchange, integrated over the selected line and viewing direction.
Volume-integrated power transferred from a coherent electromagnetic wave to an ion population, with population resolution and mode aggregation defined by each specific instance.

Ion heat convection velocity is the effective vector velocity whose product with ion thermal-energy density gives the convective flux of ion thermal energy. As a species-level intensive quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all ion charge states and is not assumed to equal the bulk ion flow velocity.
Angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to a thermal plasma population when fast or nonthermal particles undergo thermalization.
Line-of-sight-integrated bulk velocity of impurity ions, with components describing their plasma flow rather than a locally resolved velocity.
Smallest value of total magnetic field magnitude on each nested toroidal flux surface, used in determining the magnetic trapping condition for charged particles in bounce motion.
Diamagnetic-drift contribution to an area-normalized momentum-balance source, representing pressure-gradient-driven transport of a specified projected linear momentum.
Effective Fickian transport coefficient relating neutral-species particle flux to neutral-species number-density gradients, with directional components represented by more specific quantities.

Volume-integrated rate of neutron production from fusion reactions in the plasma, summed over all neutron-producing reaction channels and all reacting-population classes, including thermonuclear, beam-thermal, and beam-beam contributions.

Normalized momentum flux due to E cross B drift is the dimensionless vector form of toroidal-momentum transport in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame carried by electrostatic E cross B motion after division by a reference momentum-flux scale. It does not imply a particular projection relative to the magnetic field.
Dimensionless vector describing magnetic-field perturbations relative to a positive reference magnetic-field scale.
Flux-surface-averaged current density carried parallel to the magnetic field by the inductive ohmic-drive contribution.
Field-aligned projection of the effective neutral population velocity in a specified internal quantum state, retaining only its diamagnetic-drift contribution.
Signed ratio of the plasma flow component along the local magnetic-field direction to the local plasma sound speed.
Effective parallel diffusivity for transporting momentum by the aggregate neutral population along magnetic-field lines.

Poloidal component of the effective convection velocity for particle transport of a specified neutral internal state, serving as the advective coefficient multiplying the state number density in the poloidal direction of flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
Signed effective velocity governing the poloidal convective transport of particle density associated with a specified neutral internal state in the edge plasma.
Effective coefficient relating the radial diffusive flux of electron particles to the radial gradient of electron number density in magnetized-plasma transport.
Effective Fickian coefficient relating the outward radial diffusive flux of charge-state-summed ions to the gradient of their total particle density.
Effective coefficient relating neutral-particle diffusive flux to the radial gradient of neutral number density, with outward transport directed toward the last closed flux surface.
Radial Fickian diffusion coefficient governing cross-field transport of thermal energy carried by a specified ion charge state.
Residual magnetic-field strength at the plasma position during initiation, produced by imperfect cancelation of external coil fields and capable of inhibiting electron-avalanche breakdown.
Time rate of change of the total volume-integrated thermal internal energy of the plasma, representing the net power surplus or deficit in the global thermal energy balance.
Thermal electron absorbed wave power is the total coherent-wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population, integrated over the plasma volume.
Thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to thermal electrons by Coulomb collisions with fast particles.

Volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer to thermal ions of a specified charge state from non-Maxwellian source populations, aggregated over all guiding-center orbit classes of the source particles.
Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, without restricting orbit class or spatial direction.
Angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume deposited in thermal ions when fast particles undergo thermalization.

Thermal plasma internal energy rate is the signed time derivative of the plasma’s stored thermal internal energy. It is positive during net thermal-energy accumulation and negative during net thermal-energy loss.
Toroidal component of the net angular-momentum source density acting on a specified ion charge state.
State-resolved diffusivity governing down-gradient transport of neutral-particle momentum along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.

Toroidal component of the volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque on thermal ions of a selected charge state, giving the net rate of toroidal angular momentum transfer to that ion population by collisions.

Toroidal thermal-ion torque density due to thermalization is the flux-surface-averaged transfer rate per unit volume of toroidal angular momentum to thermal ions due to fast-particle thermalization. The toroidal direction is the increasing-φ direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
Toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered by Coulomb collisions to trapped fast ions interacting with a specified ion charge state.
Toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume from Coulomb collisions to trapped thermal ions in a specified charge state, projected in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
Effective velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport of total plasma momentum, distinct from the plasma bulk flow velocity.

Total thermal plasma internal energy is the internal energy stored in the thermal motion of the plasma's thermal particle populations, integrated over the plasma volume. It is the global stored thermal energy reservoir of the plasma; its time rate of change is a separate tendency quantity, distinct from any individual heating, transport, or radiation channel.
Trapped current density is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux associated with trapped-particle transport, including its collisional drag back-current.
Trapped fast-particle current density is the vector electric current density carried by fast particles on magnetically trapped orbits, excluding compensating electron and thermal-ion return currents.
Trapped fast-electron collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to the trapped fast-electron population through Coulomb collisions.

Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, restricted to trapped-orbit contributions and without restricting spatial direction.
Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated by the Lorentz force, averaged over a magnetic flux surface for trapped particles.
Variation of length of an interferometer beam is the signed plasma-induced optical path length difference relative to the no-plasma reference for the same beam path.
Signed direction cosine of a sensor’s oriented measurement direction projected onto the x axis of the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
Signed direction cosine of a sensor’s oriented measurement direction along the z axis in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
Line-integrated electron density measured along a diagnostic line-of-sight.
Straight field line poloidal angle coordinate on the 2D wave propagation grid
Poloidal cross‑sectional area of a magnetic flux surface
Minimum value of the safety factor profile, indicating the location of the most rational flux surface.

Volumetric rate at which energy density is added to or removed from a specific neutral species quantum state by atomic and collisional processes. It is the state-resolved neutral energy source term, with positive values denoting net energy gain by that state.
Poloidal convective velocity for neutral state momentum transport
Toroidal torque density transferred to the thermal particle population from Coulomb collisions with electrons, evaluated using the co-passing part of the distribution function.
